title: Software Engineer - Postgres Tooling
text:
ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Software Engineer, Postgres Tooling to join our CLI team and help build the open-source tools developers use to change their Postgres schemas safely. You’ll join as a co-maintainer of pg-delta, our schema diff and migration engine, and grow into leading it.

Given two databases, or a database and a folder of SQL files describing the schema you want, pg-delta works out the differences and generates the migration to get from one to the other. It powers supabase db diff, db pull, and declarative schemas, and it runs underneath Supabase’s platform, branching, and AI agent workflows. Every migration it generates is verified on a throwaway clone before it’s trusted, and it’s tested against 331 scenarios on PostgreSQL 14–18. We’re now working toward a stable, standalone 1.0 release for any Postgres developer, on Supabase or not.

This is a correctness-first role. The SQL this tool generates runs against production databases, so privilege safety and avoiding data loss are non-negotiable. It’s a great fit for someone who loves Postgres at the catalog level, enjoys compiler-style problems, and thrives in async, fast-paced environments.




WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

In this role, you’ll:

 - Co-maintain pg-delta: review and merge changes, including PRs written by AI agents, and grow into its lead maintainer.

 - Own correctness: triage bug reports from GitHub and support, fix diff and dependency-ordering bugs, and extend test coverage across Postgres versions.

 - Make sure generated migrations are privilege-safe and never silently lose data, by detecting destructive changes and rewriting them into safe equivalents where possible.

 - Help take pg-delta to a stable 1.0: a public API with a semver contract, documentation, and broader coverage of Postgres extensions.

 - Work with the open-source community: triage issues, review outside contributions, and say no gracefully when a request doesn’t fit.

 - Work with the teams across Supabase that build on pg-delta, so migrations are generated and run the same way everywhere.

 - Write the design docs and technical strategy that set the tool’s direction, working async across teams.

 - Share the CLI team’s on-call rotation. Weekdays are covered follow-the-sun, and because we ship packaged software that users can roll back, pages are rare.
   


YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

Must have:

 - Have 8+ years of experience as a software engineer, including deep, hands-on work with PostgreSQL.

 - Know Postgres internals at the catalog level: pg_catalog, pg_depend, object ownership, grants and default privileges, RLS policies, and extension membership.

 - Understand DDL and migration semantics: which changes take locks, which can’t run inside a transaction, how dependencies determine ordering, and how to spot a destructive change.

 - Treat a migration that silently loosens access as a top-severity bug.

 - Write strong TypeScript, and design tests for correctness, such as differential, property-based, or corpus testing across multiple Postgres versions.

 - Are comfortable with compiler-style problems: dependency graphs, topological ordering, cycle handling, and diffing.

 - Can confidently review complex changes in an intricate codebase, including AI-generated PRs.

 - Have owned software in production with users in the loop: staged rollouts, error monitoring, and triaging real bug reports.

 - Have led a technical project across several teams, from an ambiguous start to production.

 - Communicate clearly in writing and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

Nice to have, roughly in order of how much they’d help:

 - Have built or maintained schema diff or migration tool

title: Cybersecurity Engineer (India)
text:
We are on a mission to build the AI-native platform for finance—a multi-agent system that reimagines how investment teams make decisions and empowers them to move faster, think deeper, and operate smarter.

Security is foundational to earning the trust of financial institutions and protecting their most sensitive data. As a Cybersecurity engineer, you will play a critical role in building a secure, resilient platform—embedding security into our architecture, infrastructure, and engineering practices while enabling the team to move quickly and confidently. You'll work across application code, cloud infrastructure, and security architecture to build a secure, resilient platform without slowing down innovation.

What You’ll Do

Identify, investigate, and directly remediate security vulnerabilities in application code, APIs, infrastructure, and cloud configurations.

Write, review, and ship production-quality code to address security issues, rather than simply handing findings off to other engineers.

Design and implement secure authentication, authorization, RBAC, session management, and data protection mechanisms.

Secure our AWS and Kubernetes environments, including networking, IAM, secrets management, and infrastructure-as-code.

Conduct security reviews, threat modeling, vulnerability assessments, and penetration testing, and drive findings through remediation and verification.

Build automated security checks into CI/CD pipelines, including static analysis, dependency scanning, and infrastructure security testing.

Own security monitoring, incident detection, response, and continuous improvement of our security posture.

Drive security compliance efforts, including SOC 2, customer security assessments, and audit readiness.

Collaborate closely with backend, frontend, and infrastructure engineers to build security into the platform from the ground up.

Note: This remote position requires monthly travel to the Bay Area or Seattle for in-person team meetings.

You Might Be a Fit If You...

Have 3–7 years of experience in security engineering, software engineering, or infrastructure engineering, with substantial hands-on security experience.

Are a strong programmer who can independently navigate an unfamiliar codebase, identify vulnerabilities, implement fixes, write tests, and ship changes to production.

Have proficiency in Python or another backend programming language, with experience building or maintaining production software.

Understand common application vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10), including injection, broken access control, authentication flaws, SSRF, and insecure API design.

Have hands-on experience with AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, networking, IAM, and cloud security.

Understand authentication and authorization protocols, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and RBAC.

Have experience using security testing tools and translating findings into concrete code and infrastructure changes.

Are comfortable debugging issues across multiple layers, from frontend and backend application code to cloud infrastructure.

Understand secure development practices, automated testing, code reviews, and CI/CD pipelines.

Can independently own security issues end-to-end, from discovery and root cause analysis through implementation, testing, and verification.

Are pragmatic and execution-oriented, balancing security rigor with the speed of a growing startup.

Bonus Points

Experience building or securing fintech, financial data platforms, or enterprise SaaS products.

Experience with SOC 2, ISO 27001, penetration testing engagements, and enterprise customer security reviews.

Familiarity with TypeScript, React, PostgreSQL, and modern Python backend frameworks.

Experience with AI/LLM security, including prompt injection, agent permissions, tool misuse, and data exfiltration.

Experience implementing security automation, policy-as-code, and infrastructure-as-code.

Experience managing enterprise IT security, endpoint protection, or devic

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
text:
About Refold
Refold is building the next-generation AI platform that replaces enterprise integration and consultants. We’re pioneering autonomous AI agents that understand complex enterprise systems, generate production-ready code, and operate at a scale no consulting firm can match. Today, we’re starting with integrations—a $50B market. Tomorrow, we’re building towards a world where AI agents handle any complex cognitive work.
Traction: Serving 20+ enterprise customers with Fortune 500 deployments, processing 10M+ API calls/day. Refold was founded by Jugal Anchalia & Abhishek Kumar, who sold their previous startup to Netmeds; they have also been featured in Forbes 30 Under 30. They have experience at organisations such as Nomura, JioMart, InstaMojo, IIT Kharagpur, and IIT Roorkee. We are funded by marquee investors, including Eniac Ventures, Tidal Ventures, Karman Ventures, Ahead VC & Better Capital.
The Role:
As a forward-deployed engineer, you turn the hardest enterprise integration problems into production-grade systems on our agentic platform. You’ll take ambiguous, real-world requirements; messy APIs; undocumented systems; and edge cases nobody anticipated and reason from first principles to ship production-grade integrations.
You’re a curious, hands-on builder with a customer-first mindset and a real passion for AI already on the frontier of agentic tooling and vibe coding and eager to point that energy at real customer problems. You think like a solutions engineer: the goal isn’t to build; it’s to solve. Mostly delivery, with time as the technical engine behind our highest-stakes POCs — and the patterns you uncover shape the platform itself.

Team: Small, high-calibre technical team working directly with architects, product, and founders.

Building: Agentic AI workflows, connectors, and high-throughput integration pipelines.

You’ll work with integration leaders and engineering teams at high-growth SaaS companies and Fortune 500 enterprises.

Key Responsibilities:

Solve hard integration problems. Take ambiguous, real-world enterprise requirements and reason from first principles to design integrations that work, including the problems for which no playbook exists yet.

Build agentic workflows end-to-end. Implement complete integrations on Refold’s AI-native integration platform, orchestration logic, agentic decision-making, data transformations, and system connectivity against live enterprise systems.

Drive product direction from the field. You’re one of our highest-signal sources of product truth. Surface gaps, friction, and missing capabilities you hit while building and validate new platform features through real customer workflows.

Power high-stakes POCs. Partner with the pre-sales team to execute the technical work behind proofs-of-concept, building and validating integrations that prove value during the sales cycle.

Codify what works. Turn hard-won learnings into reference architectures, integration patterns, and runbooks that scale across the delivery team and feed the support knowledge base.

Evolve agentic capabilities. Contribute to the evolution of Refold's agentic workflows — decision-making logic, tool invocation, and autonomous execution within integrations — and feed every implementation back into the skills/graph layer so the platform's agents get measurably smarter with each integration you ship.

Required Skills & Abilities:

2-4 years in solutions engineering, integration engineering, product engineering, or a similar hands-on technical role.

A curious, hands-on builder, you reason about systems from first principles, love getting your hands dirty, and are energised by ambiguity.

Genuine passion for AI: you already build with cutting-edge tools (LLMs, agentic frameworks, and vibe coding) for fun, not just at work, and you stay on the frontier as it moves.
